title: An SL(6,C)-Based Framework for Cosmological Evolution: Spectral Constraints, Charged Condensation, and Gravitational Waves
content: We develop an effective framework that relates geometric spectral constraints, neutrino condensation, and gravitational-wave production within an SL(6,C)-based cosmological program. The construction distinguishes the 35-dimensional statistical configuration space from the proposed six-dimensional physical spacetime and the four-dimensional Lorentzian effective theory. A common derivative-coupled action determines the background equations, charge evolution, and energy balance. For a specified positive mediator operator, we derive a susceptibility bound that excludes neutral-origin spinodal condensation when the induced attraction remains subcritical. At fixed nonzero phase charge, Routh reduction instead yields a centrifugal barrier and, under explicit conditions, a unique healthy radial equilibrium. Noncollinear unstable scalar modes generate a continuous band of transverse–traceless sources; a finite-duration response and an unequal-time correlator then determine the emitted spectrum. We also characterize the infrared fixed point of a specified renormalization-group ansatz and derive conditions for maintaining a condensate phase as a local clock. The results constrain admissible effective models without fixing a unique compactification, flavor spectrum, cosmological trajectory, or gravitational-wave peak structure.
